findings.reason: the match must adopt the owner's dot-insensitive comparison (or reuse `_WORKTREE_COMPONENT`) or the census mislabels nearly every recorded failure as gone.
findings.text: §2 classifies a missing path as a worker worktree when it sits "under a `reckon-worktrees` component" and cites `_workspace_roots` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:454`) as the owner, but that convention has three owners and the live root is dotted: `_WORKTREE_COMPONENT = ".reckon-worktrees"` (`reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:239`) and `Code/.reckon-worktrees` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:780`) both carry the leading dot, and `_workspace_roots` itself matches with `part.lstrip(".") == "reckon-worktrees"` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:464`); a literal "under a `reckon-worktrees` component" equality misses the `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/...` root that the plan says 1,450 of 1,450 sampled failures sit under, so those failures would be reported as gone, and the section claims it "re-derives neither" while this fallback re-derives the match inline

findings.reason: the section must state in its own text that the new module retires or merges nothing because no owner of a Claude Code MCP-connection census exists, or name what it merges.
findings.text: §2 introduces `reckon/mcp_census.py` and its census function, which the section says agents call for another window, so the section adds to the `public_definitions` family, yet its only accounting sentence covers the CLI family

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one new module hides log enumeration, a cause-pattern table, working-directory classification and the transcript `storage-slow` walk behind one windowed function the doctor block and agents both call; the interface is smaller than the behaviour it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2's missing-path fallback re-derives the worktree-root placement convention inline and cites only one of its three owners.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1597, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 accounts for the CLI family ("adds no command and no option") but adds a new module's public census function without naming what it retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §2 cites and reuses `_in_linked_worktree` (`reckon/cli_entry.py:132`), `transcript_index` (`reckon/velocity.py:1363`) and extracts the sole `tool_result` walk in `promotion_receipts` (`reckon/velocity.py:1586`) rather than copying it; no reader of Claude Code's `mcp-logs-*` connection logs exists anywhere under `reckon/` or `tests/`, so the new module adds machinery rather than duplicating it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only layering is the extracted `reckon/velocity.py` helper both callers share, which extends the existing owner instead of wrapping it; the census module wraps no existing machinery.
